0: The Price of a Calibration Query
When an extra kind of measurement stops being an optimisation and becomes a precondition

Rider University  ·  CIG-AMF formal research programme  ·  every theorem below is machine-checked in Lean 4 (leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0-rc2, mathlib 1f495c61) with no sorry and axioms only {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}
20: A population of K·m items carries unknown values θᵢ, split into K groups; group g carries an unknown common offset b_g. The answer wanted is a threshold set: which items lie above a fixed level.
ORDINARY query on item i:  observes θᵢ + b_g(i), variance v, unit price. It sees the value and the offset only IN COMBINATION.
CALIBRATION query on group g:  observes b_g directly, variance ν, price κ.
Write a = x/v for ordinary precision on an item, b = z/ν for control precision on its group, Δ for the separation of the two worlds, s_m = √m, s_κ = √κ.
TWO QUESTIONS, AND ONLY THESE TWO
·  WHEN does the calibration query stop being an efficiency gain and become mandatory?
·  WHAT does it cost — the exact optimal value under a unit budget, not an order of magnitude?
WHAT IS NOT NEW  (read at theorem level, not from abstracts)

Dette & Titoff 2009, Thm 2.1: the T-optimal value IS the squared Chebyshev approximation error; Thm 2.2 characterises ALL T-optimal designs. Their criterion is already profiled, and the noncentrality δ² = θ₀ᵀM₁₁.₂θ₀ is a SCHUR COMPLEMENT — our I_u = D_u − M_u²/(2K) has that same shape.
Bennouna et al. 2025, Thm 1: a dataset is sufficient iff Δ(X,C) ⊆ span D — existential, over a PREDEFINED query set.
So profiling, the Schur shape, closed-form criterion values and identifiability are CITED, not claimed. Neither prior prices a query TYPE, states a necessity dichotomy, or gives a rate in (K, m, κ).
8: 1.  Exhibit a configuration on which every ordinary query is blind, so the attainable value is exactly zero — a dichotomy, not a slow rate.
2.  Prove the exact optimal value once a calibration query is bought, matched on both sides and attained.
3.  Certify on one explicit instance that no anchor-free design can match an anchored one, in exact rationals.
4.  State the novelty boundary on the front of the poster, not in an appendix.

Every ordinary query has the SAME mean in both worlds, and the answers differ. So the calibration query is not an improvement — it is a precondition.

27: THE LAW IS EXACT, AND THE NUMERICS AGREE TO MACHINE PRECISION.  Two independent optimisers over the same feasible set reproduce the closed form in all 32 cells, worst relative gap 2.5 × 10⁻¹⁶. Nelder–Mead never exceeds it, which is the direction that would falsify an upper bound.

THE COST OF A MISSING QUERY TYPE IS TOTAL; THE COST OF BAD ALLOCATION IS BOUNDED.  Over the same 32 cells, removing the controls gives EXACTLY zero — not a numerical shortfall but the hidden-shift witness of step 1, verified before the solver is called. A uniform design that keeps all controls still reaches 73.5–100% of the optimum (median 91.7%).

That asymmetry is the practical message. An experimenter who allocates badly loses a bounded fraction. An experimenter who omits the query type loses everything, and no amount of sampling recovers it.

13: A calibration query is not an efficiency improvement a good allocator could do without. There are configurations on which every ordinary query has identical means in two worlds with different answers, so the value is exactly zero until a query of the new type is bought.
Once bought, its price is EXACT: the constant 1/(2K(√m+√κ)²) is matched by a lower bound, an upper bound over all unit-budget designs, and an attaining design.

SCOPE — NOT ESTABLISHED.  (1) Common v, ν, κ and equal gaps; heterogeneous cases are not covered. (2) Step 7 certifies ONE instance. (3) Step 1 exhibits two indistinguishable worlds, it does not characterise all of them. (4) No estimator and no finite-sample guarantee is claimed.
